# Temple Scroll Column 61 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 61 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**61:1** When you march out to fight your enemies and I, the LORD your God, hand them over to you and you take prisoners from among them,

**61:2** if you notice among the captives a beautiful woman and are drawn to her, wishing to marry her,

**61:3** you must bring her into your home. She is to shave her head and cut her nails.

**61:4** She must take off the clothes she was wearing when captured and live in your house, mourning her father and mother for an entire month.

**61:5** After that, you may sleep with her and she will become your wife.

**61:6** If later you are no longer pleased with her, you must let her go free. You must never sell her for money.

**61:7** You must not exploit her, since you have already taken advantage of her.

**61:8** Suppose a man has two wives — one he loves and one he does not — and both bear him sons,

**61:9** but the firstborn belongs to the wife he does not love. When the time comes to pass on his property to his sons,

**61:10** he must not give the rights of the firstborn to the son of the wife he loves over the actual firstborn, the son of the wife he does not love.

**61:11** He must recognize the true firstborn — the son of the unloved wife — by giving him a double share of everything he owns,

**61:12** because that son was the first sign of his father's strength. The rights of the firstborn belong to him.

**61:13** If a man has a son who is stubborn and defiant, refusing to obey either his father or his mother,

**61:14** and even after they discipline him he still refuses to listen, then his father and mother must take hold of him and bring him before the elders at the town gate.

**61:15** They are to say to the elders: This son of ours is stubborn and defiant. He refuses to obey us. He is a wastrel and a drunk.

**61:16** Then all the men of the town must stone him to death. In this way you will purge evil from among you, and all Israel will hear of it and be afraid.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 61 rewrites Deuteronomy 21:10–21 as God speaking directly. The shift to first person is the Temple Scroll's signature theological move — God does not need Moses as intermediary. "Exploit" captures the sense of tyrannical treatment. "Wastrel" for זולל conveys dissolute living more vividly than the traditional "glutton."*
